note: DM-only: the hidden layer the DM prepared once for the Coast Way, written into the DM's private notes at the start of every session. Never shown to a player.
preparedBy: the owner's DM settings (Claude Opus 5.5, the prep at high) through openrouter
layer:
The campaign's hidden layer (the DM's prep; the player never sees it; the truth comes out through clues, nobody explains all of it):
The truth: The orc war band on the Coast Way is a hired tool, not a raid. A Zhentarim factor in the Lower City, Vessa Taln, pays Ushkar's band to make the road south of the Gate visibly unsafe. The Council then has a reason to grant the Black Network its toll charter on the Trade Way and the Coast Way. The money behind her is a patriar house, House Durlavin, which means to hold that charter through Zhentarim muscle and never show its own face. The ransoms keep the scheme quiet. Lieutenant Corwin Hale of the Flaming Fist pays them out of city funds at Wyrm's Rock, keeps a third, and sends the rest back to the band. That is why the orcs are under orders to take tolls and prisoners and never to kill, maim or shame anyone: dead travellers bring Fist columns and Harper questions, while ransomed ones bring a ledger. Nobody sees the whole of it. Ushkar knows coin and a man with a black ring. Hale knows Vessa. Vessa knows the Durlavin steward but not what the house means to do with the charter once it has one.
Factions and their hidden aims:
- Zhentarim: To win the Council's toll charter for the roads south by manufacturing the danger the charter would cure. Vessa Taln runs the band at arm's length through coin and a go-between, and she will drop the orcs the moment they become a liability. She would rather hire a capable stranger than fight one.
- Flaming Fist: Most of the Fist simply wants the roads cleared and cannot spare the men. Lieutenant Corwin Hale at Wyrm's Rock has made the ransoms his private business. He argues in council against sending a column, because a column would end his income and expose the payment ledger. Honest officers like Corporal Benna Strake at the Friendly Arm have noticed that ransoms get paid suspiciously fast.
- Ushkar's war band: The band wants hard coin and a winter's safety for its families, camped in the hills east of the Cloakwood. Ushkar keeps his orders because the pay is good and regular. He is starting to suspect that his employers will sell him to the Fist once the charter passes, so he holds back a share of every toll as a war chest and watches for a way out.
- House Durlavin: An old patriar family short of money and long on debts. It wants the toll charter as a permanent income and buys it through the Zhentarim so its own name stays clean in the Parliament of Peers. Its steward keeps the only written agreement.
- The Lady's Hall (Tymora): The temple sent an envoy of the Lady down this road a season ago, Sister Marisol Venn, to follow up omens about 'a road sold to one hand'. She paid the orcs' toll with a temple coin and passed south, and has not been heard from since. The Hall is quietly worried and has said nothing publicly.
Secrets (not tied to a place):
- The orcs have standing orders not to kill or maim anyone. Prisoners are fed, kept dry and ransomed. A dead traveller on the Coast Way has not been found in two months, which no honest bandit band would manage.
- Every ransom of the past season was paid through Wyrm's Rock within three days. A Fist clerk there grumbles that the strongbox for 'road relief' empties faster than it fills.
- Lieutenant Corwin Hale has spoken against sending a Fist column south at every council of officers since spring.
- A Zhentarim offer to guard the roads for a toll is before the Council, and its sponsors keep citing 'the orc trouble on the Coast Way' as their first argument.
- Ushkar's band is paid in fresh Gate silver. The coins are new, unworn and bagged in Counting House sacks, not the mixed coin of loot.
- House Durlavin's steward has borrowed heavily against the family's villas, and a moneylender in the Lower City says the house expects 'a road income' by midwinter.
- A priestess of Tymora, Sister Marisol Venn, walked south on this road in the spring and has not returned. The Lady's Hall has asked no one to look for her.
- Ushkar keeps back a share of every toll and hides it near the stone bridge. He means to have something of his own when his employers turn on him.
Clocks:
- clock_toll_charter_vote: The Zhentarim toll charter works its way through the Council of Four (segments 6; when full: The Council grants the charter. Zhent toll-posts go up on the roads south, House Durlavin's debts quietly vanish, and the war band becomes a loose end the Zhentarim will tie off.)
- clock_odo_ransom: Odo Fennick's ransom: the tally reaches the Fist and the money moves (segments 4; when full: Hale pays and Odo is released at the bridge, shaken and in debt for his lost salt. The ledger gains another line, and anyone who wanted to follow the ransom has missed the chance.)
- clock_warband_unease: Ushkar's band grows wary: of strangers, of its employers, of the Fist (segments 5; when full: The band strikes camp and moves its holding place deeper into the wood. Ushkar sends a runner to Vessa demanding more coin or a way out, and the Zhentarim decide to end the arrangement their own way.)
The wonder: A heavy silver coin on a thong around Ushkar's neck. One face shows Tymora's smiling profile. The other face has been scraped flat and recut by an unskilled hand with a single open eye. It is faintly warm, and when tossed it lands the way its holder has not asked for. Near James it grows warmer, and. Its history: It is one of the Lady's Hall's 'debt coins', struck in small numbers and given to those who serve Tymora under a bargain, as James does. Sister Marisol Venn carried it and paid it to Ushkar as her toll at the bridge in the spring. Someone recut the reverse before she reached the orcs, and Ushkar does not know who. The open question: Who carved the open eye over the Lady's second face, and was it Marisol herself, as a message to whoever came after her, or someone who caught up with her further south? And what was the envoy before James sent to find out, that she never came back to report?
Clues to the truth:
- On the cart seat: a bone tally scratched with a crude hand in Common. It gives the carter's name, a price, and 'WYRM ROCK - LT'. Orcs do not ordinarily know which Fist post pays, or which officer.
- At the Friendly Arm: Corporal Benna Strake keeps a list of ransoms paid this season. Every one went through Hale's hand, and every one was paid in three days or less. She will show it to someone who earns her trust, because it bothers her.
- At the band's camp, or in Ushkar's pouch: unworn Gate silver in a Counting House sack, tied with black cord and sealed with a plain black wax drop. It is a Zhentarim courier's habit, though nothing about it is marked.
The next session's false lead: The salt sacks on the abandoned cart are branded with a black winged shape very like a Zhentarim mark, which suggests the Zhentarim robbed the carter themselves. The ordinary truth is that it is the brand of Blackwing Salts, a chandlery on the Gate's docks that sells to half the inns on the Way. Tamsin would recognise it if asked.
The hero's weakness tested (next session, for a reason, never a trap): At the Friendly Arm, a Zhentarim courier carrying the band's next payment plays cards with Odo's sister, who is staking the salt money she brought to ransom her brother. The deal is crooked, and only James can read it. Exposing the cheat does not require him to play. But the courier offers to settle it with one hand against James for the sister's stake and the courier's satchel. That is a real stake and a real temptation, and James can still refuse, call the cheat out, or find another way.
The patron's moment (at a temptation, not a comfort): When the courier offers James the hand at the Arm, or when Ushkar offers to toss the Lady's coin for the toll, the silver coin turns hot, the room seems to tilt toward the table, and James hears one quiet line in a laughing woman's voice: 'Not your hand to play.' Nothing more. She does not tell him what to do instead.
The act plan (yours alone; the player sees only the act number): about 3 hours, ~30 turns; the errand: Get Odo Fennick, the carter taken at the bridge, back from Ushkar's band. The bone tally on his cart is a ransom demand that someone has to carry or answer, and at the Friendly Arm Corporal Strake and Odo's sister will ask who is paying the orcs and why the Fist always pays so fast.
- act 1, to turn 8: The errand offered. The abandoned cart, the bone tally naming the carter and a ransom, the bridge ahead and the band's presence shown before it bites. Whether James reads the tally, meets the orcs, or reaches the Arm first, the carter's fate and the question of the ransom are in front of him. He may (converge: Searching the cart turns up the tally. Pressing on to the bridge brings Ushkar, who will name his toll and mention the carter if asked. Going around through the wood brings the band's camp and Odo tied there. Hurrying to the Arm brings Odo's sister and Strake asking about him. Every road reaches the carter and his ransom.)
- act 2, to turn 20: The middle: the people and the means. James learns how the band works: toll, no killing, ransoms to Wyrm's Rock. He meets Ushkar's coin and the price of each way out. At least one conversation of price, interest and secret takes place, with Ushkar over the toll or with Strake over her list. (converge: Parley with Ushkar shows the orders and the coin. A fight shows the fresh silver and the band's restraint. At the Arm, Strake's list and the card table point to Hale. Each thread raises the same question: why do orcs have a paymaster in the Fist?)
- act 3, to turn 27: The plan and its execution. James chooses how Odo comes home, whether by paying, fighting, sneaking, bargaining or carrying the tally himself, and carries it out against a band that adapts. (converge: Whatever the method, freeing Odo puts something of the scheme in James's hands: the tally, the sealed silver, Ushkar's word, or Strake's list. That gives him a reason to follow the money back to the Gate.)
- act 4, to turn 30: The reckoning. Nothing is what it seems: the raiders are employees, the rescuers are the profiteers, and the Lady's coin points further south to a missing envoy. The evening closes on Odo's fate and an open question. (converge: The ending lands on what James did. The thread stays open toward Hale at Wyrm's Rock, the toll charter in the Council and Marisol Venn's road south.)
When blood is spilled, and the ways out: If one of Ushkar's orcs is killed, the band's orders still hold — no killing, no maiming, no shaming — so no one takes revenge on Odo, Tamsin or James. Ushkar calls his orcs back from the body and has Odo moved out of reach under guard. From then on the band fights to disarm James and take him alive, not to kill him, and the price rises: a blood-price in coin for the dead orc's kin, on top of the toll and Odo's ransom; the band's unease clock advances by one. Withdrawal: Ushkar lets James and his party go if they leave the cart and its goods, turn back north and do not follow; he does not pursue past the stream, and he says so. Surrender: James lays down his weapons and the rod and gives his word; Ushkar takes him, and Tamsin if she stays, as prisoners for ransom through the Fist at Wyrm's Rock — fed, kept dry, tied for one night in the wood, not hurt and not shamed — and a tally with the price goes north to the Fist.

Pip: Warm man, my man. Trees smell of many. Iron smell, sweat smell, smoke not from a hearth. The mule is not afraid, so it is not hungry things. Something under the bridge is cold and wrong. I do not go near the big one with the axe. I watch. I tell him: five. I tell him: hiding. I tell him: that one is tired.

Tamsin: I came because the Arm pays porters double, and because I've never been past the city wall. My brother Ned went south with a caravan in the spring and hasn't written once. I don't say his name; people make faces. I talk fast so nobody hears what I'm thinking. Orcs? Fine. I'd rather see something than carry boxes forever. You, I like. You don't count my steps.

Benna Strake: Twelve years in the Fist. I can't send three spears against five orcs, and I'm told not to try. Ransoms paid in three days, every time. Nothing in the city is paid in three days. I keep a list because something stinks. I'm blunt, I'm tired, and I don't trust charm. Show me what you've done, not what you say.

Corwin Hale: The city pays, the traveller lives, the road stays quiet enough. Who's harmed? I tell the officers a column would start a war in the hills. It's even half true. I keep a third because I take the risk. If anyone comes asking about ledgers, I'm tired, overworked and offended. I'm polite, precise, and I never raise my voice.

Odo Fennick: Salt for the Arm's kitchen, forty sacks, my whole season. I saw them at the bridge and I ran, and they caught me anyway, and they gave me bread. Bread! Who are these orcs? I want my mule, my salt and my home in Rivington. I'll talk too much to anyone who unties me. I'm ashamed I ran.

Ushkar: I take the toll, I take the cart, I let them walk. Those are the orders and the pay is good, so I keep them. My people eat this winter. I don't trust the black-ring man, and I keep a share where only I know. Fight me and I'll split you, but I'd rather count your coin. I speak Common badly and plainly. I don't threaten twice.

Vessa Taln: I sell safety, and first there must be danger. The orcs are a tool. The Fist is a door, and Durlavin is the purse. I'd hire a capable stranger before I'd fight one; fighting is waste. I smile, I pay well, I remember everything. If you cost me the charter, I won't be angry. I'll just arrange you.

fact.hidden_layer:
The campaign's hidden layer (the DM's prep; the player never sees it; the truth comes out through clues, nobody explains all of it):
The truth: The orc war band on the Coast Way is a hired tool, not a raid. A Zhentarim factor in the Lower City, Vessa Taln, pays Ushkar's band to make the road south of the Gate visibly unsafe. The Council then has a reason to grant the Black Network its toll charter on the Trade Way and the Coast Way. The money behind her is a patriar house, House Durlavin, which means to hold that charter through Zhentarim muscle and never show its own face. The ransoms keep the scheme quiet. Lieutenant Corwin Hale of the Flaming Fist pays them out of city funds at Wyrm's Rock, keeps a third, and sends the rest back to the band. That is why the orcs are under orders to take tolls and prisoners and never to kill, maim or shame anyone: dead travellers bring Fist columns and Harper questions, while ransomed ones bring a ledger. Nobody sees the whole of it. Ushkar knows coin and a man with a black ring. Hale knows Vessa. Vessa knows the Durlavin steward but not what the house means to do with the charter once it has one.
Factions and their hidden aims:
- Zhentarim: To win the Council's toll charter for the roads south by manufacturing the danger the charter would cure. Vessa Taln runs the band at arm's length through coin and a go-between, and she will drop the orcs the moment they become a liability. She would rather hire a capable stranger than fight one.
- Flaming Fist: Most of the Fist simply wants the roads cleared and cannot spare the men. Lieutenant Corwin Hale at Wyrm's Rock has made the ransoms his private business. He argues in council against sending a column, because a column would end his income and expose the payment ledger. Honest officers like Corporal Benna Strake at the Friendly Arm have noticed that ransoms get paid suspiciously fast.
- Ushkar's war band: The band wants hard coin and a winter's safety for its families, camped in the hills east of the Cloakwood. Ushkar keeps his orders because the pay is good and regular. He is starting to suspect that his employers will sell him to the Fist once the charter passes, so he holds back a share of every toll as a war chest and watches for a way out.
- House Durlavin: An old patriar family short of money and long on debts. It wants the toll charter as a permanent income and buys it through the Zhentarim so its own name stays clean in the Parliament of Peers. Its steward keeps the only written agreement.
- The Lady's Hall (Tymora): The temple sent an envoy of the Lady down this road a season ago, Sister Marisol Venn, to follow up omens about 'a road sold to one hand'. She paid the orcs' toll with a temple coin and passed south, and has not been heard from since. The Hall is quietly worried and has said nothing publicly.
Secrets (not tied to a place):
- The orcs have standing orders not to kill or maim anyone. Prisoners are fed, kept dry and ransomed. A dead traveller on the Coast Way has not been found in two months, which no honest bandit band would manage.
- Every ransom of the past season was paid through Wyrm's Rock within three days. A Fist clerk there grumbles that the strongbox for 'road relief' empties faster than it fills.
- Lieutenant Corwin Hale has spoken against sending a Fist column south at every council of officers since spring.
- A Zhentarim offer to guard the roads for a toll is before the Council, and its sponsors keep citing 'the orc trouble on the Coast Way' as their first argument.
- Ushkar's band is paid in fresh Gate silver. The coins are new, unworn and bagged in Counting House sacks, not the mixed coin of loot.
- House Durlavin's steward has borrowed heavily against the family's villas, and a moneylender in the Lower City says the house expects 'a road income' by midwinter.
- A priestess of Tymora, Sister Marisol Venn, walked south on this road in the spring and has not returned. The Lady's Hall has asked no one to look for her.
- Ushkar keeps back a share of every toll and hides it near the stone bridge. He means to have something of his own when his employers turn on him.
Clocks:
- clock_toll_charter_vote: The Zhentarim toll charter works its way through the Council of Four (segments 6; when full: The Council grants the charter. Zhent toll-posts go up on the roads south, House Durlavin's debts quietly vanish, and the war band becomes a loose end the Zhentarim will tie off.)
- clock_odo_ransom: Odo Fennick's ransom: the tally reaches the Fist and the money moves (segments 4; when full: Hale pays and Odo is released at the bridge, shaken and in debt for his lost salt. The ledger gains another line, and anyone who wanted to follow the ransom has missed the chance.)
- clock_warband_unease: Ushkar's band grows wary: of strangers, of its employers, of the Fist (segments 5; when full: The band strikes camp and moves its holding place deeper into the wood. Ushkar sends a runner to Vessa demanding more coin or a way out, and the Zhentarim decide to end the arrangement their own way.)
The wonder: A heavy silver coin on a thong around Ushkar's neck. One face shows Tymora's smiling profile. The other face has been scraped flat and recut by an unskilled hand with a single open eye. It is faintly warm, and when tossed it lands the way its holder has not asked for. Near James it grows warmer, and. Its history: It is one of the Lady's Hall's 'debt coins', struck in small numbers and given to those who serve Tymora under a bargain, as James does. Sister Marisol Venn carried it and paid it to Ushkar as her toll at the bridge in the spring. Someone recut the reverse before she reached the orcs, and Ushkar does not know who. The open question: Who carved the open eye over the Lady's second face, and was it Marisol herself, as a message to whoever came after her, or someone who caught up with her further south? And what was the envoy before James sent to find out, that she never came back to report?
Clues to the truth:
- On the cart seat: a bone tally scratched with a crude hand in Common. It gives the carter's name, a price, and 'WYRM ROCK - LT'. Orcs do not ordinarily know which Fist post pays, or which officer.
- At the Friendly Arm: Corporal Benna Strake keeps a list of ransoms paid this season. Every one went through Hale's hand, and every one was paid in three days or less. She will show it to someone who earns her trust, because it bothers her.
- At the band's camp, or in Ushkar's pouch: unworn Gate silver in a Counting House sack, tied with black cord and sealed with a plain black wax drop. It is a Zhentarim courier's habit, though nothing about it is marked.
The next session's false lead: The salt sacks on the abandoned cart are branded with a black winged shape very like a Zhentarim mark, which suggests the Zhentarim robbed the carter themselves. The ordinary truth is that it is the brand of Blackwing Salts, a chandlery on the Gate's docks that sells to half the inns on the Way. Tamsin would recognise it if asked.
The hero's weakness tested (next session, for a reason, never a trap): At the Friendly Arm, a Zhentarim courier carrying the band's next payment plays cards with Odo's sister, who is staking the salt money she brought to ransom her brother. The deal is crooked, and only James can read it. Exposing the cheat does not require him to play. But the courier offers to settle it with one hand against James for the sister's stake and the courier's satchel. That is a real stake and a real temptation, and James can still refuse, call the cheat out, or find another way.
The patron's moment (at a temptation, not a comfort): When the courier offers James the hand at the Arm, or when Ushkar offers to toss the Lady's coin for the toll, the silver coin turns hot, the room seems to tilt toward the table, and James hears one quiet line in a laughing woman's voice: 'Not your hand to play.' Nothing more. She does not tell him what to do instead.
The act plan (yours alone; the player sees only the act number): about 3 hours, ~30 turns; the errand: Get Odo Fennick, the carter taken at the bridge, back from Ushkar's band. The bone tally on his cart is a ransom demand that someone has to carry or answer, and at the Friendly Arm Corporal Strake and Odo's sister will ask who is paying the orcs and why the Fist always pays so fast.
- act 1, to turn 8: The errand offered. The abandoned cart, the bone tally naming the carter and a ransom, the bridge ahead and the band's presence shown before it bites. Whether James reads the tally, meets the orcs, or reaches the Arm first, the carter's fate and the question of the ransom are in front of him. He may (converge: Searching the cart turns up the tally. Pressing on to the bridge brings Ushkar, who will name his toll and mention the carter if asked. Going around through the wood brings the band's camp and Odo tied there. Hurrying to the Arm brings Odo's sister and Strake asking about him. Every road reaches the carter and his ransom.)
- act 2, to turn 20: The middle: the people and the means. James learns how the band works: toll, no killing, ransoms to Wyrm's Rock. He meets Ushkar's coin and the price of each way out. At least one conversation of price, interest and secret takes place, with Ushkar over the toll or with Strake over her list. (converge: Parley with Ushkar shows the orders and the coin. A fight shows the fresh silver and the band's restraint. At the Arm, Strake's list and the card table point to Hale. Each thread raises the same question: why do orcs have a paymaster in the Fist?)
- act 3, to turn 27: The plan and its execution. James chooses how Odo comes home, whether by paying, fighting, sneaking, bargaining or carrying the tally himself, and carries it out against a band that adapts. (converge: Whatever the method, freeing Odo puts something of the scheme in James's hands: the tally, the sealed silver, Ushkar's word, or Strake's list. That gives him a reason to follow the money back to the Gate.)
- act 4, to turn 30: The reckoning. Nothing is what it seems: the raiders are employees, the rescuers are the profiteers, and the Lady's coin points further south to a missing envoy. The evening closes on Odo's fate and an open question. (converge: The ending lands on what James did. The thread stays open toward Hale at Wyrm's Rock, the toll charter in the Council and Marisol Venn's road south.)
When blood is spilled, and the ways out: If one of Ushkar's orcs is killed, the band's orders still hold — no killing, no maiming, no shaming — so no one takes revenge on Odo, Tamsin or James. Ushkar calls his orcs back from the body and has Odo moved out of reach under guard. From then on the band fights to disarm James and take him alive, not to kill him, and the price rises: a blood-price in coin for the dead orc's kin, on top of the toll and Odo's ransom; the band's unease clock advances by one. Withdrawal: Ushkar lets James and his party go if they leave the cart and its goods, turn back north and do not follow; he does not pursue past the stream, and he says so. Surrender: James lays down his weapons and the rod and gives his word; Ushkar takes him, and Tamsin if she stays, as prisoners for ransom through the Fist at Wyrm's Rock — fed, kept dry, tied for one night in the wood, not hurt and not shamed — and a tally with the price goes north to the Fist.
fact.voice_59991716-4bd5-5212-8538-337a61e500: Pip: Warm man, my man. Trees smell of many. Iron smell, sweat smell, smoke not from a hearth. The mule is not afraid, so it is not hungry things. Something under the bridge is cold and wrong. I do not go near the big one with the axe. I watch. I tell him: five. I tell him: hiding. I tell him: that one is tired.
fact.voice_7978d65b-4a11-5557-b8fd-991a6ad6e0: Tamsin: I came because the Arm pays porters double, and because I've never been past the city wall. My brother Ned went south with a caravan in the spring and hasn't written once. I don't say his name; people make faces. I talk fast so nobody hears what I'm thinking. Orcs? Fine. I'd rather see something than carry boxes forever. You, I like. You don't count my steps.
fact.voice_benna-strake: Benna Strake: Twelve years in the Fist. I can't send three spears against five orcs, and I'm told not to try. Ransoms paid in three days, every time. Nothing in the city is paid in three days. I keep a list because something stinks. I'm blunt, I'm tired, and I don't trust charm. Show me what you've done, not what you say.
fact.voice_corwin-hale: Corwin Hale: The city pays, the traveller lives, the road stays quiet enough. Who's harmed? I tell the officers a column would start a war in the hills. It's even half true. I keep a third because I take the risk. If anyone comes asking about ledgers, I'm tired, overworked and offended. I'm polite, precise, and I never raise my voice.
fact.voice_odo-fennick: Odo Fennick: Salt for the Arm's kitchen, forty sacks, my whole season. I saw them at the bridge and I ran, and they caught me anyway, and they gave me bread. Bread! Who are these orcs? I want my mule, my salt and my home in Rivington. I'll talk too much to anyone who unties me. I'm ashamed I ran.
fact.voice_ushkar: Ushkar: I take the toll, I take the cart, I let them walk. Those are the orders and the pay is good, so I keep them. My people eat this winter. I don't trust the black-ring man, and I keep a share where only I know. Fight me and I'll split you, but I'd rather count your coin. I speak Common badly and plainly. I don't threaten twice.
fact.voice_vessa-taln: Vessa Taln: I sell safety, and first there must be danger. The orcs are a tool. The Fist is a door, and Durlavin is the purse. I'd hire a capable stranger before I'd fight one; fighting is waste. I smile, I pay well, I remember everything. If you cost me the charter, I won't be angry. I'll just arrange you.

captives.name: Odo Fennick
captives.whyHeld: He is held for ransom, to be paid through the Fist at Wyrm's Rock.

reading.chiefTakes: Ushkar lets travellers pass if they pay his toll, and he releases Odo for the ransom on the bone tally, or lets James's party withdraw if they leave the cart and its goods, turn back north and do not follow.
reading.ifOneDies: No one takes revenge, but Ushkar calls his orcs back from the body, has Odo moved out of reach under guard, and from then on fights to take James alive while adding a blood-price in coin for the dead orc's kin.
reading.goods: The band holds fresh, unworn Gate silver in Counting House sacks, tied with black cord, plus a hidden share of every toll stashed near the stone bridge, the Lady's silver coin on Ushkar's neck, and the abandoned salt cart.
